commit.message:
Phase 6b: attachments, transactional outbox and notifications (#7)

* Phase 6b: attachments, transactional outbox and notifications

- Attachments upload straight from the browser to S3-compatible storage with pre-signed PUTs
  (size, type and disposition signed); the API verifies the stored object before exposing it,
  issues 60-second download links, and a worker job removes abandoned uploads
- Type allow-list (no HTML/SVG/script types), 10 MB and 50-per-issue limits, sanitised names,
  random storage keys, Content-Disposition: attachment
- Transactional outbox: issue assignment and comments write events in the same transaction;
  the worker relay publishes them with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, LISTEN/NOTIFY wake-ups and a
  500 ms poll fallback, using deterministic job IDs
- Notifications: idempotent fan-out (per-recipient dedupe key) to assignees, reporters and
  commenters; assignment email; list, unread count, mark read and read-all endpoints
- Web: attachments panel with progress, notification bell (30 s polling) and notifications page
- SeaweedFS replaces MinIO locally and in Testcontainers (ADR-0011): MinIO images are no
  longer published
- Tests: unit, HTTP integration against Postgres + Redis + SeaweedFS, mutation-checked relay
  locking, dedupe and upload verification; web component tests; browser run


* Fix notification list failing on seeded rows; match seed payload to worker

The development seed wrote notifications in an older payload shape, so GET /notifications
failed for seeded users (Sam, Alex). The seed now writes the same payload the worker does,
and the list skips (and logs) any row it cannot parse instead of failing the request.


---------

Phase 6a: issues, workflow, board, comments and history (#6)

- Issue contracts in @forge/types: status workflow, request/response schemas, key parsing
- API: create/list/search/get/update/delete issues with per-project numbering, optimistic
  locking (409 on stale version), workflow validation, resolvedAt tracking, change history,

  page with inline editing, sidebar fields, Markdown comments and history
- Tests: unit, HTTP integration against real Postgres + Redis, web component tests
- Docs: API reference, security notes, README status

commit.message:
Phase 5: project management (projects, members, labels, settings) (#5)

API
- Projects: create (creator becomes project manager), list (members;
  admins see all; name-ordered keyset pagination, search, archived
  filter), get by id or key, update, archive/restore, admin-only
  permanent delete gated on archived state and a repeated key
- Members: add by email with a role, change role, remove, leave;
  role changes apply on the next request (ACL cache invalidated); the
  last project manager can't be demoted or removed, with a row lock so
  concurrent demotions can't both succeed (mutation-tested)
- Labels: CRUD, names unique per project case-insensitively
- Guard: archived projects are read-only for every write except
  restore; new label and project-key scopes
- Permission matrix moved to @forge/types, shared by API and web
- Audit: project lifecycle and membership events; project.updated
  records only fields that actually changed

Web
- Projects list with search and active/archived toggle, create form
  with key suggestion, project workspace (overview, members, labels,
  settings incl. archive/restore and admin delete), role-aware
  controls, confirmation dialogs; home page lists your projects

Tests: types 90, api 58 unit + 13 HTTP + 107 integration, web 34;
browser run of 14 project-management steps as manager and non-member.

commit.message:
Phase 4: authentication, sessions and role-based access control (#4)

API
- Register, login, refresh, logout, logout-all, password reset by
  email, profile and password change (FR-1), admin user management
  (FR-2.1), project permission matrix and guard (ADR-0002)
- ES256 access tokens via @nestjs/jwt with pinned algorithm/issuer/
  audience; opaque refresh tokens stored hashed, rotated on every use,
  family revoked on replay, 409 for benign two-tab races
- Redis revocation cutoff so deactivation, demotion, password change and
  logout-everywhere take effect on the next request (ADR-0010)
- Account and IP lockout, Redis fixed-window rate limits with IETF
  RateLimit headers, breached-password check (HIBP k-anonymity), equal
  timing for unknown emails, CSRF Origin check on cookie endpoints
- Global auth guard (secure by default), Zod validation with field
  errors, append-only audit entries for every security event
- BullMQ email queue plus a separate worker process (nodemailer, Mailpit
  locally); reset links removed from Redis after delivery

Web
- Login, register, forgot/reset password, signed-in shell; access token
  in memory only, single-flight refresh on 401, proxy.ts redirects

Found by testing and fixed
- Referer from the reset page carried the reset token into API logs:
  request logs now use an allow-list; reset page sends no-referrer and
  strips the token from the URL

Docs: api.md, security.md, ADR-0010. Tests: api 114 unit + 13 HTTP +
88 integration (Postgres + Redis via Testcontainers), web 20; browser
run of every flow including the emailed reset link.

commit.message:
Phase 3: database schema, migrations and seed data (#3)

* Phase 3: database schema, migrations and seed data

PostgreSQL schema for the whole platform in Prisma 7 (34 tables),
one reviewed initial migration, a transactional seed, and integration
tests against a real Postgres + pgvector.

- Schema: identity, projects, issues (+ history, labels, comments,
  attachments, links), sprints with membership history, notifications,
  append-only audit log, outbox, GitHub, RAG documents/chunks, AI tables
- Integrity enforced in the database: composite FKs that make
  cross-project labels/sprints/chunks impossible, partial unique indexes
  (one ACTIVE sprint per project, one current sprint per issue), CHECKs
  for status/timestamp consistency and formats, audit-log triggers
  that reject UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE
- Search: generated tsvector columns + GIN, trigram title index, HNSW
  cosine index on vector(1536); schema mirrors these so migrate diff
  reports no drift (checked in tests and CI)
- Gap-free per-project issue numbers via a row-locking allocator
- forge_ai NOLOGIN role limited to RAG tables; compose creates its
  login from env, no password in migrations
- API: PrismaService (pg driver adapter), database readiness check;
  readiness no longer returns raw driver errors (they named internal
  hosts), full errors are logged instead
- Seed: 6 users, 2 projects, 3 sprints, 17 issues with comments and
  status history; single transaction; refuses to run in production
- CI: compose job migrates, checks drift, seeds twice, checks AI role
- docs/database.md: ER diagrams and the reasoning for each rule

Tests: api 26 unit + 9 HTTP + 58 integration (Testcontainers).


* Generate the Prisma client on install

The compose CI job failed at `prisma db seed` with "Cannot find module
'../src/generated/prisma/client'": the client is gitignored and was
only generated by Turbo's db:generate task, which the job's direct
prisma commands bypass. The README's setup steps (install, db:deploy,
db:seed) had the same gap on a fresh clone.

A postinstall `prisma generate` in apps/api (Prisma's recommended
setup) makes every `pnpm install` leave a usable client. The Turbo task
stays, so schema edits still regenerate before lint/typecheck/test.

Verified by replaying the compose job from a fresh clone: install,
migrate deploy, no-drift diff, seed, no-op second seed, AI role checks.


---------

commit.message:
Phase 2: repository structure and configuration (#1)

Monorepo (pnpm workspaces + Turborepo) with three runnable services and
shared packages, local infrastructure and CI.

- apps/api: NestJS 11 skeleton with zod-validated env, pino JSON logs
  with request-ID propagation and credential redaction, RFC 9457
  problem+json errors, helmet, CORS allow-list, Swagger, Redis client,
  and /health/live + /health/ready with per-check timeouts
- apps/web: Next.js 16 + Tailwind 4 + TanStack Query; same-origin /api
  rewrite; status card showing live API readiness
- apps/ai-service: FastAPI app factory, pydantic-settings, structlog,
  request-ID middleware, constant-time service-token auth; uv, ruff,
  strict mypy, pytest with warnings as errors
- packages/types (shared zod schemas), packages/ui (shadcn/ui),
  packages/config (tsconfig, ESLint flat config, Prettier)
- docker-compose: Postgres 16 + pgvector, Redis 7 (AOF), Mailpit, all
  with healthchecks; init script adds extensions and a test database
- CI: TypeScript, Python and Compose jobs; Dependabot; PR template
- ADR-0009: NestJS 11 / TypeScript 5.9 / ESLint 9 and why

Tests: api 21 unit + 8 HTTP (Supertest), web 3, types 7, ai-service 16.
Verified end to end against the real containers, including readiness
going to 503 and recovering when Redis is stopped and restarted.

Phase 1: requirements and architecture

Add the planning baseline the later phases build against:

- docs/requirements.md: problem statement, per-project roles and
  permission matrix, functional requirements FR-1..FR-13 (MoSCoW),
  measurable non-functional requirements, scope, 20-phase plan
- docs/architecture.md: modular monolith + worker + AI service,
  transactional outbox, sync vs async split, auth flow, OWASP and
  OWASP LLM threat mapping, permission-aware hybrid RAG, AWS
  deployment and cost choices, observability, API conventions;
  8 Mermaid diagrams, all rendered with mermaid-cli to check them
- docs/adr/0001..0008: the key decisions and rejected alternatives
